summary: Oregon Dept. of Forestry lookout on Foreman Point, Wasco County: first tower 1936-37, timber replacement 1951-52, now gone. Sources disagree on dates.

facts.design: 14-foot pole live-in tower (1937 per register); later timber tower, 40 or 41 ft, dated 1951-52
facts.status_note: The replacement timber tower is gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the site.

events.note: About 40-foot laminated timber tower, about 184 man-hours of labor (dated c.1936)
Lookout fireman Paul Dennis stationed at the tower, September 1936
14-foot pole live-in tower built by the Oregon Department of Forestry
41-foot treated timber L-4 tower (date given by the register only)
Timber replacement tower dated 1952: 41 ft per Forest Fire Lookout Association, 40 ft with 14x14 cab per Rex's page
Station called four first discoveries in the fire season
Station called two first reports this season
Cab wired for electricity at 220 volts; only 110-volt service supplied
Gas stove installed in the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Fire Lookout Association date a 14-foot pole live-in tower to 1937. The Rex's page dates a 40-foot laminated timber tower to about 1936 and records a lookout stationed there in September 1936, which fits the earlier date. The story reports both.

Register: 41-foot L-4 tower in 1951. Forest Fire Lookout Association: 41-foot L-4 tower in 1952. Rex's page: 40-foot timber tower with 14x14 cab in 1952. The story reports 1951 or 1952 and 40 or 41 feet.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 12.2 is kept: it matches the 40-foot tower on the Rex's page; the register and FFLOS say 41 ft (about 12.5 m). Access is not stated by any source, so no access key. Status gone is confirmed by sources 1, 3 and 4. The Rex's page ends with a bare 'Removed' and no date, so no removed event. The Rex's header files the site under Mount Hood National Forest; the register does not. No photos added: no image URLs were captured from the cached pages. The brief's coordinates match the register.
